grants.Program Focus:
OPENING SUMMARY — WEEK OF OCTOBER 12 – 16, 2026

Week at a Glance:

A light week. Federal postings in the window were dominated by NIH research announcements and the Office of Justice Programs' FY 2026 solicitations; no new DOE, DOT, USDA, HUD, EPA, Interior or DOL NOFOs posted, California portals added nothing new, and the Federal Register carried no 2 CFR 200 or grants-policy actions (Congress is in pre-election recess; the continuing resolution runs through December 11). The items worth attention are a two-year NOAA NESDIS BAA, a BJA election-integrity program open to counties and cities, a NOAA coastal-flood research competition that earlier digests missed and whose letter of intent is due November 9, NYSERDA's offshore-wind predevelopment program, and a set of EPA and IRS compliance changes that touch utility, industrial, water and CCS clients.

Coastal Resilience Research:

NOAA NCCOS Advancing Coastal Flood Protection (NOAA-NOS-NCCOS-2026-32934) — posted September 25 and missed by the last two digests. One to six projects of up to $2,000,000 each (about $500,000 per year, up to four years) for natural-infrastructure flood protection work on public-private partnerships, insurance products and sediment management. Open to universities, nonprofits, state, local and tribal governments and for-profits; research teams must include regional users. Letter of intent due November 9, 2026; full proposals due February 12, 2027.

Earth-Observation and Satellite R&D:

NOAA FY 2027-2028 Broad Agency Announcement administered by NESDIS (NOAA-NESDIS-NESDISPO-2027-33921) — standing two-year BAA for research, education, outreach and innovative projects across every NOAA line office (satellites and data, fisheries, ocean service, weather, OAR) that fall outside NOAA's competitive programs, plus CESU projects. Rolling submissions, grants and cooperative agreements, no cost share, amounts not stated. Universities, nonprofits, companies, state, local and tribal governments eligible; CESU projects limited to non-federal CESU partner institutions. Open through September 30, 2028.

Election Administration:

BJA FY 2026 Integrity in American Elections Grant Program (O-BJA-2026-172793) — new program for state and local prosecutors and justice agencies to prevent, investigate and prosecute voter-roll and voter-fraud offenses. $5,000,000 total, up to $250,000 per award, 20 awards over 24 months from January 2027; states, counties, cities, special districts and tribes only; no match; state and local applicants must file the NOFO's Appendix 1 certification or be denied. Grants.gov December 1, 2026, JustGrants December 8.

Justice Research (Universities and Research Nonprofits):

NIJ FY 2026 Crime and Justice Research (O-NIJ-2026-172801) — $5,500,000, nine awards, workforce effectiveness, operational readiness and safety technology in adult criminal justice plus one assessment of the COPS de-escalation training program; due November 16, 2026. NIJ FY 2026 Research and Evaluation on School Safety (O-NIJ-2026-172796) — $5,000,000, six cooperative agreements evaluating anonymous reporting systems and threat-assessment teams; due November 23, 2026 (JustGrants November 30). Both open to universities, nonprofits, local governments, tribes and companies; no match.

Youth and Community Programs (Local Governments, Tribes, Nonprofits):

Four OJP programs posted October 9, all due in mid-November with no match: OJJDP Opioid Affected Youth Initiative (O-OJJDP-2026-172748, $8,920,000, up to $750,000, 12 awards; due November 16); OJJDP Strategies to Support Children Exposed to Violence (O-OJJDP-2026-172752, $7,335,000, up to $815,000, nine awards; due November 16); OJJDP Mentoring for Youth Impacted by Opioids (O-OJJDP-2026-172743, $16,500,000; local sites up to $650,000, statewide and regional up to $2,000,000, 15 awards; due November 16); and SMART Support for Adam Walsh Act Implementation (O-SMART-2026-172794, up to $400,000, about 50 awards; states and federally recognized tribes only; due November 25, JustGrants December 9). Outside GMA's core sectors but open to general-purpose local governments and tribes; suited to a short campaign to city, county and tribal contacts.

Offshore Wind and Grid Modernization (New York):

NYSERDA Offshore Wind Project Predevelopment Program (OSWPON26-1) — issued October 9; applications accepted continuously through December 31, 2029 or until funds are committed; funding levels and eligibility are in the PON documents, which did not render this run. NYSERDA Grid Modernization Utility Challenge – National Grid (PON 6240) — up to $3,000,000 for an AI-supported battery-storage health-monitoring demonstration in National Grid's New York territory; Round 1 due November 10, 2026.

Policy & Compliance Updates:

EPA moved the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program deadline for reporting year 2025 from October 30, 2026 to March 10, 2027 (interim final rule, comments due November 30) while it reconsiders the program. EPA delayed Clean Water Act hazardous-substance facility response plans from June 2027 to June 1, 2030 and removed climate-change and environmental-justice language. Executive Order 14435 directs Treasury to defer federal diesel excise taxes and suspend dyed-diesel penalties from October 5 through December 31, 2026. EPA granted Colorado Class VI (CO2 injection) primacy effective November 12. HHS proposed a second round of Administration for Native Americans grant-rule streamlining (comments due November 13, 2026). IRS opened a paperwork-renewal comment period for the Section 48C advanced energy project credit (due December 14), a signal the program will keep being administered. No Treasury or IRS energy-credit guidance (45, 45Y, 48, 48E, 45X) issued this week.

Watch List / Upcoming:

NSF X-Labs — From Sequence to Function (bioengineering): NSF released the topic announcement on October 16 (after this window) under its $1,500,000,000 X-Labs Other Transactions initiative; proposals go through SAM.gov and the X-Labs portal, and NSF's pages state no deadline (a university limited-submission notice for the same topic cites Phase 0 awards up to $1,500,000 and Phase 1 up to $50,000,000 per year, with X-Labs required to be institutionally independent, domestic, full-time teams; a Phase 0 award can run through a lead host organization). Q&A webinar November 18, 2 p.m. ET; RFI on future topics due October 30. The companion topic Artificial Intelligence for Physical Systems opened September 16 and was not covered in earlier digests. Angle: research universities and bioengineering or ag-biotech companies able to stand up an independent team; confirm the deadline and the Autonomy Factor Assessment rules on SAM.gov before outreach. DOE CMEI/AFFO notice of intent (DE-FOA-0003648, for NOFO DE-FOA-0003649) is now on Grants.gov with a listing close date of April 26, 2027 and no NOFO date; three topics (stable biomass intermediates, commodity chemicals and fuels from alternative feedstocks in existing refineries, hydrogen–natural gas blending pilot sites). EPA FY 2027 Brownfields Assessment, RLF and Cleanup solicitations are still expected this fall (about $64,000,000; up to $500,000 community-wide assessment and cleanup, $1,000,000 coalition, states and tribes, and RLF; no Multipurpose round; applications due about 60 days after posting; 20% match for Cleanup and RLF). NSF Major Research Instrumentation: the July 2025 notice scheduled a submission window of October 15 – November 16, 2026, but NSF 23-519 is archived and the updated FY 2027 solicitation had not posted as of NSF's September 17 page update; confirm before advising research clients. Department of War SBIR/STTR FY 2027 Release 1 (25 topics: Air Force 16, Navy 6, OSD 2, Army 1) pre-released October 7, opens October 28 and closes November 25 per consultant trackers; verify at DSIP before outreach. USDA Rural Development held an October 13 webinar on the updated REAP; pull the recording for the new program parameters and watch for the first application window under the final rule. USGS posted master cooperative agreements for Cooperative Ecosystem Studies Unit partners (Californian, Pacific Northwest, Rocky Mountain, Colorado Plateau and others; due November 14) — relevant only to universities that host or join a CESU. NASA ROSES A.15 Biosphere added a PI-meeting travel requirement (Step-2 due November 6). New Jersey BPU closed the CHP–Fuel Cell incentive to new applications October 9. CEC GFO-25-603 (NEVI community charging): the CEC page showed November 20, 2026 after Addendum 4 last week but did not render this run; the Master Calendar still shows October 16 — confirm. CEC Business Meeting October 19 and CPUC/CEC EPIC investment-plan workshop October 20. Appropriations: the continuing resolution (P.L. 119-103) and the surface-transportation extension expire December 11, 2026; Section 157 blocks OMB's proposed 2 CFR rewrite through that date, and the extension does not restore IIJA advance appropriations, so FY 2027 DOT discretionary NOFOs remain stalled. Next expected: Brownfields NOFOs; first REAP window notice; SIPPRA final NOFO; HUD ICDBG (NOFO December 16); CEC CORE FY 2026-27; Texas THIVE; DoW SBIR Release 1 at DSIP.

grants.Description: NOAA National Centers for Coastal Ocean Science — Advancing Coastal Flood Protection through Public-Private Partnerships, Innovative Insurance Products, and Improved Sediment Management (FY 2027 Competitive Research Program)

grants.Eligible Applicants: U.S. institutions of higher education, nonprofits, state and local governments, tribal governments, U.S. territories and Pacific Island institutions, and for-profit organizations (per the Grants.gov synopsis as mirrored; NOAA announcement does not restate eligibility). grants.Description: Bureau of Justice Assistance — OJP FY 2026 Integrity in American Elections Grant Program
grants.Agency / Funder: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Justice Programs, Bureau of Justice Assistance. Contact: OJP Response Center, OJP.ResponseCenter@usdoj.gov, 800-851-3420.
grants.Award Range: Up to $250,000 per award; 20 awards expected; 24-month period of performance starting January 1, 2027 (NOFO). The Grants.gov listing shows $5,000,000 in the award field, which is the program total.
grants.Eligible Applicants: State governments, county governments, city or township governments, special district governments, federally recognized tribal governments, and other general-purpose units of local government only. Nonprofits and universities are not eligible. State and local applicants must submit the certification in the NOFO's Appendix 1; applications without it are denied (tribes exempt). Review the certification's terms before advising California jurisdictions — last week's BJA Justice Reinvestment NOFO carried an immigration-cooperation certification that some jurisdictions will not sign. Applicants may submit more than one application for different projects.
grants.Deadline: Grants.gov (SF-424) December 1, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET; JustGrants full application December 8, 2026, 8:59 p.m. ET.
grants.Program Focus: Funds state and local prosecutors and justice agencies to prevent, investigate and prosecute voter-roll and voter-fraud offenses (illegal registration, voting by non-citizens, deceased or duplicate voters). A new Byrne JAG-authority program with a closed applicant pool of general-purpose governments and tribes. Allowable activities are investigating and prosecuting state or local election crimes and preventing offenses such as voting-system tampering and circumvention of eligibility rules. Fit for county district attorneys, county registrars working with prosecutors, city attorneys and tribal courts; at $250,000 the right scale is a dedicated investigator or analyst position plus records tools. Politically sensitive: position it as election-administration integrity and records modernization. Action: a short note to county and city contacts with a prosecutor's office after checking the certification; seven weeks is enough for a competitive application.
grants.Cost Share / Match: None (listing states no cost sharing requirement).

grants.Description: EPA — Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program: Reporting Year 2025 Deadline Extended to March 10, 2027 (Interim Final Rule)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Air and Radiation
grants.Effective Date: Effective October 14, 2026; comments due November 30, 2026; petitions for review due December 14, 2026.
grants.Summary: Moves the GHGRP reporting deadline for reporting year 2025 from October 30, 2026 to March 10, 2027. EPA says it needs time to finalize its September 2025 reconsideration proposal, which would among other things eliminate RY2025 reporting for most source categories, and that the e-GGRT system would not be ready. The underlying reconsideration is not final; EPA may retain, revise or rescind the obligations. About 8,200 reporters are affected (power generation, refineries, oil and gas systems, chemicals, cement, iron and steel, landfills, CO2 injection sites).
grants.Who It Affects: Utilities, landfill operators, industrial facilities and CCS projects that report under 40 CFR 98; also any applicant that cites GHGRP data as an emissions baseline in grant or tax-credit applications (45Q, DOE industrial decarbonization, CEC programs).
grants.GMA Action Items: Tell reporting clients the October 30 deadline no longer applies. Advise clients whose grant or 45Q strategies rely on GHGRP baseline data that the data stream may become voluntary or stop after the reconsideration is finalized, and identify substitute baselines (CARB MRR for California facilities). No comment recommended unless a client depends on continued reporting.

grants.Description: EPA — Clean Water Act Hazardous Substance Facility Response Plans: Compliance Date Delayed to June 1, 2030 (Final Rule)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Land and Emergency Management
grants.Summary: Delays by three years the deadline for covered facilities to prepare CWA hazardous-substance facility response plans, with parallel changes for newly regulated, newly constructed and event-triggered facilities. Removes climate change from the adverse-weather and hazard-evaluation provisions and replaces environmental-justice language with 'potentially exposed or susceptible populations.' EPA estimates $18–26 million per year in avoided cost. Affected NAICS include 221 (utilities) and 921/924 (government).
grants.Who It Affects: Water and wastewater utilities, ports, industrial facilities and public agencies storing CWA hazardous substances above 40 CFR 118.3 thresholds near navigable waters.
grants.GMA Action Items: Note for water-utility and port clients that FRP preparation can be deferred and budgeted later. Resilience and hazard-mitigation grant narratives should not cite this rule as a compliance driver; use state requirements and insurer expectations instead.

grants.Description: Executive Office of the President — Executive Order 14435, Emergency Tax Relief on Diesel Fuel
grants.Issuing Agency: Executive Office of the President (directs Treasury/IRS, DOT/FMCSA and USDA)
grants.Effective Date: Signed October 5, 2026; published October 9; relief period October 5 – December 31, 2026; Treasury directed to act within five days.
grants.Summary: Directs Treasury to determine whether section 7508A relief applies and, if so, to defer federal diesel excise taxes incurred October 5 through December 31, 2026 without penalty or interest, suspend penalties for highway use of dyed diesel for the same period, issue implementing guidance, and explore legislation forgiving the deferred amounts. FMCSA is told to maintain safety enforcement; USDA to coordinate dyed-diesel supply; the White House intergovernmental office to urge states to adopt matching relief. The order does not address Highway Trust Fund revenue or grant programs.
grants.Who It Affects: Transit and school-bus operators, public-works and utility fleets, agricultural producers, fuel distributors; state DOTs indirectly through Highway Trust Fund receipts.
grants.GMA Action Items: Flag to transportation, agriculture and fleet clients as a near-term cost benefit and watch for the IRS implementing notice (not in IRB 2026-42). Watch any lame-duck forgiveness bill for Highway Trust Fund offsets that could touch formula programs.

grants.Description: HHS Administration for Children and Families — Further Reducing Bureaucracy and Burden from the Administration for Native Americans (Proposed Rule)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families, Administration for Native Americans
grants.Summary: Second-stage streamlining after the June 2026 final rule that removed most of 45 CFR 1336. Consolidates the five remaining sections: drops duplicative definitions, removes the restated 20 percent match requirement from regulation (the statutory match at 42 U.S.C. 2991b(c) still applies) and trims match-waiver documentation text, routes ineligibility and suspension, termination and non-continuation appeals to the HHS Departmental Appeals Board under 2 CFR 200.339–343, and shifts financial-requirement detail to training and technical assistance. Tribes were consulted in August 2026.
grants.Who It Affects: Federally recognized tribes, Alaska Native villages and corporations, Native Hawaiian organizations and Native nonprofits applying to ANA Social and Economic Development Strategies, language and environmental programs.
grants.GMA Action Items: Tribal clients should confirm the statutory 20 percent match is unchanged in practice and consider commenting by November 13 on match-waiver documentation, which affects small tribes most. The appeals change matters for any client facing an ANA termination or non-continuation.

grants.Description: EPA — Colorado Underground Injection Control Program: Class VI Primacy (Final Rule)
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Water
grants.Summary: Grants the Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission primary enforcement authority for Class VI geologic CO2 sequestration wells under Safe Drinking Water Act section 1422; EPA retains Class VI permitting on Indian lands in Colorado and oversight. Colorado joins North Dakota, Wyoming, Louisiana, West Virginia and Arizona among states with Class VI primacy. The rule does not mention 45Q or the IIJA section 40306 primacy grant.
grants.Who It Affects: Carbon capture and storage developers; ethanol, cement, power and industrial facilities in Colorado; tribes in Colorado (the Southern Ute Tribe commented on the Indian-lands definition).
grants.GMA Action Items: For Colorado CCS and 45Q clients, Class VI permitting moves to the state after November 12; update DOE CarbonSAFE and 45Q project timelines. Treat continued primacy approvals as a signal for California clients that state-led Class VI permitting (CalGEM) remains the long-term path.

grants.Description: IRS — Information Collection Comment Request: Qualifying Advanced Energy Project Credit (Section 48C(e))
grants.Issuing Agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Internal Revenue Service
grants.Summary: IRS seeks a no-change three-year extension of the information collection for the section 48C(e) allocation program (concept paper, application, certification of property and placed-in-service notice; 5,000 estimated responses at 6.35 hours each). The notice cites Round 2 (Notice 2024-36) and describes the program's $10 billion allocation with $4 billion reserved for energy communities. It does not announce a new allocation round.
grants.Who It Affects: Manufacturers, critical-minerals and materials processors, and industrial decarbonization projects holding 48C allocations; prospective applicants if a future round is funded.
grants.GMA Action Items: Remind 48C awardees of the two-year certification and placed-in-service filing obligations. Treat the renewal as a mild signal that the program will keep being administered; no action on new rounds. GMA does not provide tax opinions — route questions to the client's tax advisor.

grants.Description: Executive Office of the President — Proclamation 11072, National Energy Dominance Month, 2026
grants.Effective Date: Signed October 7, 2026; designates October 2026. Policy signal only; no requirements.
grants.Summary: Recites the administration's energy agenda: rescission of the endangerment finding, federal land openings, more than $1 billion committed to coal and 100-plus coal plants kept open, the end of the LNG export pause, nuclear investment, grid-permitting streamlining and the March 2026 'Ratepayer Protection Pledge.' Names no programs, agencies or grants. It confirms the framing federal energy reviewers are working under: reliability, affordability, nuclear, gas, grid and domestic production rather than climate.
grants.Who It Affects: All applicants to DOE, USDA energy, DOT electrification and related federal programs.
grants.GMA Action Items: Use reliability, affordability, energy-security and domestic-supply-chain language in federal energy narratives; keep climate framing for CEC, CPUC and other state programs. No compliance step.
